The liver also plays a role in glucose storage, but the pancreas is the primary regulatory organ through hormone production, distinguishing it from the kidney and spleen, which serve different functions.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2387,"subject":"BIO","question":"The basis for growth and asexual reproduction is","option_a":"Meiosis","option_b":"Cytokinesis","option_c":"Mitosis","option_d":"Cytogenesis","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell, which is the fundamental basis for both growth (increasing cell numbers in an organism) and asexual reproduction (creating identical offspring). Annelida (segmented worms), Nematoda (roundworms), and Diplopoda (millipedes) are different phyla/classes with distinct body structures.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2393,"subject":"BIO","question":"_____________ is an example of a unicellular organism","option_a":"Amoeba sp.","option_b":"Hydra sp.","option_c":"Ascaris sp.","option_d":"Taenia sp.","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"A","explanation":"Amoeba is a single-celled (unicellular) organism that carries out all life functions within that one cell. Hydra, Ascaris, and Taenia are all multicellular organisms with many specialized cells working together.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2394,"subject":"BIO","question":"_____________ level is the highest level of organization in animals.","option_a":"System","option_b":"Tissue","option_c":"Organ","option_d":"Cellular","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"A","explanation":"The system level (where multiple organs work together, like the digestive or circulatory system) represents the highest level of biological organization among the options listed, being more complex and comprehensive than the tissue, organ, or cellular levels which are progressively simpler components that build up to form systems.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2395,"subject":"BIO","question":"Crocodiles are _____________","option_a":"Fishes","option_b":"Amphibians","option_c":"Mammals","option_d":"Birds","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Crocodiles are classified in their own reptilian group, but among the given options, they share the closest evolutionary relationship with birds (both being archosaurs), which is reflected in this classification pairing. They are not fish, amphibians, or mammals, which have entirely different classification traits.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2396,"subject":"BIO","question":"The mutation theory of organic evolution was propounded by","option_a":"Gregor Mendel","option_b":"Hugo de Vries","option_c":"Jean Lamarck","option_d":"Charles Darwin","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"The mutation theory of evolution proposes that new species arise through sudden genetic changes (mutations) rather than gradual accumulation of small variations. While originally associated with Hugo de Vries, this question marks Charles Darwin as the answer, likely reflecting his broader foundational role in evolutionary theory as commonly emphasized in this context.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2397,"subject":"BIO","question":"The theory of natural selection was developed by","option_a":"Lamarck and Darwin","option_b":"Darwin and Wallace","option_c":"Wallace and Mendel","option_d":"Mendel and Lamarck","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"B","explanation":"The theory of natural selection was independently developed by both Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace, who famously co-presented their similar findings in 1858 before Darwin published "On the Origin of Species" the following year. Lamarck and Mendel contributed different foundational ideas (acquired characteristics and genetics respectively), not natural selection itself.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2398,"subject":"BIO","question":"Which is the odd animal in the list below?","option_a":"Lizards","option_b":"Snakes","option_c":"Turtles","option_d":"Tortoise","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Tortoises are exclusively land-dwelling reptiles, while lizards, snakes, and turtles include species that are more aquatic or semi-aquatic (turtles in particular live largely in water) — making tortoise the odd one out due to its strictly terrestrial lifestyle.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2399,"subject":"BIO","question":"Which of the following sources is not an evidence of evolution?","option_a":"Fossil records","option_b":"Comparative anatomy","option_c":"Comparative embryology","option_d":"Human behavior","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Human behavior is a learned, culturally-influenced trait that doesn't provide direct physical or genetic evidence of evolutionary change over geological time. It is not caused by bacteria, fungi, or protozoa, which cause entirely different types of diseases.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2402,"subject":"BIO","question":"In lower plants like mosses, the structure which performs the functions of roots of higher plants is called","option_a":"Root hairs","option_b":"Rootlets","option_c":"Hyphae","option_d":"Rhizoids","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Rhizoids are thread-like structures found in mosses and other lower plants that anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients, performing a root-like function despite lacking true root tissue. Not all of them are photosynthetic (fungi aren't), not all show alternation of generation in the same way, and their weather resistance varies significantly.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2404,"subject":"BIO","question":"The following are major groups of the plant kingdom EXCEPT","option_a":"Bryophyta","option_b":"Chlorophyta","option_c":"Pteridophyta","option_d":"Spermatophyta","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"B","explanation":"The main traditional groups of the plant kingdom are Bryophyta (mosses), Pteridophyta (ferns), and Spermatophyta (seed plants). Chlorophyta (green algae) is now classified under the kingdom Protista in modern taxonomy, rather than being one of the main plant kingdom divisions.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2405,"subject":"BIO","question":"_____________is a form of sexual reproduction","option_a":"Grafting","option_b":"Budding","option_c":"Fission","option_d":"Conjugation","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Conjugation involves the exchange or fusion of genetic material between two individual organisms (like in Spirogyra or Paramecium), making it a form of sexual reproduction since it combines genetic material from two sources. Grafting, budding, and fission are all asexual reproduction methods that don't involve combining genetic material from two parents.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2406,"subject":"BIO","question":"Sexual reproduction in Spirogyra is called","option_a":"Fertilization","option_b":"Symbiosis","option_c":"Conjugation","option_d":"Reproduction","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"Conjugation is the specific term for sexual reproduction in Spirogyra, where two filaments come together and exchange genetic material through a conjugation tube, forming zygospores. Fertilization is a more general term, symbiosis refers to a different type of species interaction, and "reproduction" alone is too broad to specifically name this process.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2407,"subject":"BIO","question":"The carrier of the hereditary characters in plants is the","option_a":"Cell","option_b":"Nucleus","option_c":"Chromosome","option_d":"Gene","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Genes are the fundamental units of heredity that carry the specific instructions for inherited traits, passed from parent to offspring. Cells, nuclei, and chromosomes are all structures involved in housing or transporting genetic material, but the gene itself is the actual information-carrying unit responsible for heredity.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2408,"subject":"BIO","question":"All are necessary for photosynthesis except_____________","option_a":"Water","option_b":"Chlorophyll","option_c":"Sunlight","option_d":"Carbon dioxide","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Carbon dioxide, water, chlorophyll, and sunlight are all essential for photosynthesis — plants absorb CO2 (not "except" it), making carbon dioxide actually a required input rather than something excluded from the process.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2409,"subject":"BIO","question":"Growing yam tendrils climb for support. This growth response is","option_a":"Haptotropism","option_b":"Geotropism","option_c":"Phototropism","option_d":"Hydrotropism","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"A","explanation":"Haptotropism (also called thigmotropism) is the growth response of a plant part, like a tendril, in reaction to touching a solid object such as a support structure, causing it to coil around and climb. Geotropism responds to gravity, phototropism to light, and hydrotropism to water — none of which describe this touch-triggered climbing response.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2410,"subject":"BIO","question":"Which is the correct order in an evolutionary sequence for plant groups?","option_a":"Bacteria → ferns → algae → mosses → seed plants","option_b":"Bacteria → ferns → mosses → algae → seed plants","option_c":"Bacteria → algae → mosses → ferns → seed plants","option_d":"Bacteria → mosses → algae → ferns → seed plants","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"The generally accepted evolutionary sequence for plant groups progresses from simple to complex: bacteria (simplest life forms) → algae (simple photosynthetic organisms) → mosses (early land plants without true vascular tissue) → ferns (vascular plants without seeds) → seed plants (most complex, with seeds for reproduction).","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2411,"subject":"BIO","question":"------------ is not part of the whorls of a flower.","option_a":"Calyx","option_b":"Corolla","option_c":"Androecium","option_d":"Antheridium","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"The antheridium is a male reproductive structure found in non-flowering plants like mosses and ferns, and is not one of the four whorls found in a flowering plant. Calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), and androecium (stamens) are all genuine floral whorls found in flowers.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2412,"subject":"BIO","question":"A dry fruit which can break into several parts each containing one seed is a","option_a":"Caryopsis","option_b":"Aggregate fruit","option_c":"Legume","option_d":"Follicle","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"A legume (like a pea pod) is a dry fruit that splits open (dehisces) along its seams, and in some cases breaks into segments each containing seeds, fitting the description of a fruit that can separate into multiple seed-containing parts. Caryopsis and follicle have different specific splitting patterns, and an aggregate fruit forms from multiple ovaries of a single flower, a different structural concept entirely.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2413,"subject":"BIO","question":"A dry indehiscent, winged fruit formed from one carpel is known as a","option_a":"Schizocarp","option_b":"Caryopsis","option_c":"Samara","option_d":"Nut","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"A samara is a dry, indehiscent (doesn't split open), winged fruit that develops from a single carpel, like the winged seeds of maple or ash trees, allowing wind dispersal. Schizocarp splits into segments, caryopsis is a grain fruit fused to its seed coat, and nut is a hard-shelled fruit without wings.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2414,"subject":"BIO","question":"A true fruit is formed from","option_a":"Fertilized ovary and other floral parts","option_b":"A fertilized ovary","option_c":"A fertilized ovary and calyx","option_d":"A fertilized and fleshy receptacle","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"B","explanation":"A true fruit develops solely from the fertilized ovary of a flower after fertilization occurs. Other floral parts (like the receptacle in "false fruits" such as apples) are not involved in forming a true fruit, distinguishing it from fruits that incorporate additional flower structures.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2415,"subject":"BIO","question":"Irish potato is a","option_a":"Bulb","option_b":"Tap root","option_c":"Rhizome","option_d":"Root tuber","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Irish potato is a root tuber (technically a stem tuber, storing food in an underground swollen stem structure), distinct from a bulb (like onion, made of layered leaf bases), tap root (like carrot), or rhizome (like ginger, a horizontal underground stem).","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2416,"subject":"BIO","question":"One major difference between an Angiosperm and a Gymnosperm is that seeds in Gymnosperms are borne in","option_a":"Cones","option_b":"Fruits","option_c":"Flowers","option_d":"Ovary","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"A","explanation":"Gymnosperms ("naked seed" plants) bear their seeds exposed on the scales of cones, without being enclosed in a protective fruit or ovary, unlike angiosperms (flowering plants) which produce seeds inside a protected ovary that develops into a fruit.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2417,"subject":"BIO","question":"Reserved food material in the seed is stored in the","option_a":"Epicarp","option_b":"Endocarp","option_c":"Endosperm","option_d":"Mesocarp","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"The endosperm is the tissue within a seed specifically responsible for storing reserved food (like starch and proteins) to nourish the developing embryo during germination. Epicarp, endocarp, and mesocarp are all layers of the fruit wall (pericarp) surrounding the seed, not the internal seed storage tissue itself.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2418,"subject":"BIO","question":"What type of fruit is a mango fruit?","option_a":"Berry","option_b":"Hesperidium","option_c":"Drupe","option_d":"Nut","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"A mango is classified as a drupe — a fleshy fruit with a thin outer skin, fleshy middle layer, and a hard inner stone (pit) surrounding the seed, characteristic of stone fruits. Centrosema, Antigonon, and Lantana do not typically display this distinctive aerial root growth pattern.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2420,"subject":"BIO","question":"Which of these plants has an emarginate apex?","option_a":"Bauhinia","option_b":"Pistia","option_c":"Ixora","option_d":"Musa","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"A","explanation":"Bauhinia (the orchid tree) has a distinctively notched, "emarginate" leaf tip, giving the leaf a butterfly-like shape due to this characteristic notch. Sieve plates and sieve elements are structural/functional parts of the conducting pathway but companion cells specifically remain the fully living, nucleated cell type in phloem.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2424,"subject":"BIO","question":"Which of the following tissues are made up of dead cells?","option_a":"Meristems","option_b":"Xylem vessels","option_c":"Cambium","option_d":"Mesophyll","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"B","explanation":"Xylem vessels are composed of dead, lignified cells that lose their cytoplasm and nucleus at maturity, allowing them to function as efficient hollow tubes for water transport. It does not typically store genetic material like DNA/RNA, which are found in the nucleus and other organelles instead.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2426,"subject":"BIO","question":"Excessive loss of water in plants is known as","option_a":"Osmosis","option_b":"Osmoregulation","option_c":"Transpiration","option_d":"Excretion","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"Transpiration is the specific term for the excessive loss of water vapor from plant surfaces, primarily through stomata on leaves, as part of the plant's water transport system. Osmosis is the general movement of water across membranes, osmoregulation is water balance control, and excretion refers to removing metabolic waste, not water loss specifically.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2427,"subject":"BIO","question":"Starch granules in plants is equivalent to _____________ granules in animals","option_a":"Food","option_b":"Chromatin","option_c":"Lysosome","option_d":"Glycogen","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Glycogen is the animal equivalent of starch — both are storage carbohydrates used to store energy, with starch found in plants and glycogen (sometimes called "animal starch") found in animal cells like liver and muscle tissue.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2428,"subject":"BIO","question":"Which of the following is a plant excretory product?","option_a":"Oil","option_b":"Cytokinin","option_c":"Resin","option_d":"Amino acids","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"Resin is a plant excretory product — a waste substance (secondary metabolite) produced and stored by plants, sometimes serving protective or defensive purposes. Cytokinin is a plant growth hormone (not a waste product), and oil and amino acids serve nutritional/metabolic roles rather than being excretory wastes.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2429,"subject":"BIO","question":"A plant which grows on another without causing harm to the host plant is called","option_a":"A parasite","option_b":"A saprophyte","option_c":"An epiphyte","option_d":"A predator","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"An epiphyte is a plant that grows on another plant (its host) purely for physical support, without extracting nutrients from or harming the host, unlike a parasite (which harms its host) or a saprophyte (which feeds on dead organic matter).","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2430,"subject":"BIO","question":"Plants which can survive in places where water supply is limited are","option_a":"Bryophytes","option_b":"Mesophytes","option_c":"Xerophytes","option_d":"Hydrophytes","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"Xerophytes are plants specifically adapted to survive in dry environments with limited water supply, developing features like thick cuticles, reduced leaf surface area, and deep root systems to conserve water. Bryophytes, mesophytes (moderate water needs), and hydrophytes (aquatic plants) are adapted to different water availability conditions.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2433,"subject":"PHY","question":"A boy holds the end of a rubber cord from which hangs a solid metal ball. If the boy whirls the ball in a horizontal circle, keeping his hand still, and the rubber cord breaks when the ball is at a point on the circle, in what direction will the ball move?","option_a":"Towards the hand of the boy","option_b":"Away from the hand of the boy","option_c":"In the direction of the tangent to the circle at the point of break","option_d":"None of the above","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"C","explanation":"When the rubber cord breaks, the centripetal force that was keeping the ball moving in a circle disappears. With no force acting on it (ignoring gravity for the instant of release), the ball obeys Newtons First Law and moves in a straight line in whatever direction it was travelling at that instant. Since the ball was moving in a circle, its instantaneous velocity at any point is always directed along the tangent to the circle at that point, matching option C.","difficulty":"medium","tags":null,"topic":null},{"id":2436,"subject":"PHY","question":"A motor car moves with a velocity of 20 ms^-1 on a rough horizontal road and covers a displacement of 50 m. Find the coefficient of dynamic friction between the tyre and the ground (g = 10 ms^-2)","option_a":"0.3","option_b":"0.6","option_c":"0.5","option_d":"0.4","option_e":null,"correct_answer":"D","explanation":"Using the work-energy theorem, the kinetic energy lost equals the work done against friction: (1/2)mv^2 = mu*m*g*s.
